prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The refrigerator interior lies directly in front of the camera wearer, with the wearer’s hands and forearms nearest at roughly 0.2–0.6 m, the door-side bottles around 0.4–0.8 m, and the shelves and containers roughly 0.5–1.0 m away. In frames 1–2 the raised arm extends from the lower-left foreground toward the upper shelf; in frame 3 the view turns downward and right, and in frame 4 the nearer hand reaches toward the middle/lower shelf before the view rises again in frame 5. The depth map separates the foreground arm from the shelves more clearly than RGB and shows the curved door or side wall as very near along the right edge, partly occluding the interior. It provides no evidence of another person or of anyone facing the wearer, and its distances are only rough because large bright regions at the door edge, weak object boundaries, and changing brightness across frames appear unreliable.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map identifies the wearer’s visible arm/hand as “person,” the large refrigerator interior as “refrigerator” in frames 3–5, several bottles along the left or lower-left edge, and a bowl near the upper-right area in frame 2 and near the top in frame 4. These masks make object occupancy and overlap clearer than RGB: the arm crosses in front of the appliance and shelf contents, while several bottles are clipped by the left frame boundary or partly hidden by other objects. Combined with the RGB/depth context, the arm and nearby bottles are within roughly 0.2–0.8 m of the wearer, while the bowl and deeper shelf contents are approximately 0.5–1.0 m away; segmentation itself does not measure distance. The map is unreliable where it labels most of the refrigerator as “oven” in frames 1–2, merges many shelf objects into the appliance mask, omits numerous containers, and produces fragmented black holes and inconsistent bottle masks.
descriptions.pose: The pose map detects only the camera wearer’s hands, in magenta, with no second person or visible body skeleton, so another person’s position, facing direction, or gaze is not supported. In frames 1–2 one hand is high and slightly left of center, about 0.3–0.6 m from the camera and within reach of the upper shelf; in frame 3 it shifts lower and near center as the camera turns downward, then appears farther right in frame 4 and high-right in frame 5. The articulated landmarks reveal hand orientation and finger configuration more clearly than RGB, especially where the hand overlaps similarly colored or dim refrigerator contents, and show that the hand remains in front of the shelves rather than behind them. The map is unreliable for full-body geometry because forearms, torso, and scene objects are absent, some finger landmarks appear crowded or duplicated, and apparent hand movement also includes camera rotation.
